content.summary_of_the_paper: This works deal with post-hoc explainability of CNN models for vision. Namely, authors propose a novel method for automatic concept extraction and localization for explainable AI. They differ from other methods because they provide localization where others dont. Secondly, authors propose a novel evaluation metric and synthetic datasets to support the metric. Approach is compared with two SOTA related works, achieving SOTA on the novel metrics and datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

- Novel approach for automatic concept extraction, with a new proposed pipeline that differs significantly from closest prior work, eg ACE [14]
- Concept extraction is pretty intuitive, and the whole procedure is clear. Additionally, adding localization in contrast to related works is a nice touch.
- Newly proposed benchmark for concept extraction line-of-work is a good contribution. Metrics and benchmarks for XAI are sparsely available, and it is good for the community that different approaches to evaluation are developed, especially offline ones (not involving humans in the loop). However, I do have some issues with metrics and evaluation in general, which are detailed in weaknesses bellow.
- SOTA performance on proposed benchmarks and metrics
- I quite like the computational cost analysis in Appendix F, and I think that a short conclusion from that analysis should end up in main paper. Few sentences on why one should use ECLAD over ACE or ConceptSHAP in their system.


Weaknesses:
- My main issue is with evaluation and proposed metrics. I applaud the design of new metrics, representation correctness and importance correctness, but I find the motivation on what are they measuring and why do we need them to be lacking. Usually, in interpretability, when a quantitative metric is introduced, especially around importance scores, it is used as a proxy of a particular human evaluation. Because interpretability and importances of features are evaluated via human understanding of the model. I cant seem to understand what is this novel metric capturing well that it can be used to replace a very costly human study, and help us develop models faster?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Paper is clear and easy to follow
- Work seems novel and original, differs significantly from related work
- Reproducibility is good, authors even provided code in suppl
- I have some issues with quality, I cant seem to buy motivation for the need of new metrics, and why are they good/better than existing metrics? See weaknesses for more details.
content.summary_of_the_review: I find the newly proposed metrics to be lacking motivation. However, I still find the novelty of the approach significant, and the impact to the XAI community would be good. Hence I currently vote for marginally above acceptance threshold.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
For concept-based explanations of the prediction process of CNNs, this work propose Extracting Concepts with Local Aggregated Descriptors (ECLAD) using a pixel-wise aggregation of multi-scale activation maps. 
This paper focuses on global explanation and validates concept extraction methods synthetic datasets and real-world examples.
Extensive experiments are conducted to support this method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
- This paper is well written in an easy-to-understand manner, and the motivation is clear.
- This method focuses on how CNNs represent pixels internally, and provide an automatic validation process to minimizes the need of human intervention.
- Validation of the proposed synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates robust performances of the proposed method.


Weaknesses
- The dataset is somewhat limited, and it seems to be a dataset that reflects a specific purpose to represent the real environment.
- Although the motivation is clear, the novelty of the proposed model is not clear. Why should human intervention in the validation process be reduced in this work? And it is not known how this method is automated and how much less human intervention there is than other existing verification methods. What is the speciality of the proposed ECLAD configuration?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The reason for the need to explain CNN's internal process is clear, and many experiments have shown the effect.
- Supplementary materials provide code for reproducibility.
- Due to the need for pixel-wise annotation, this work provides new synthetic datasets, but this makes it questionable whether it is applicable to the general case.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This work investigates to validate concept-based explanations of CNNs.
For this process, the author focuses on the global description by proposing a novel local aggregation descriptor method and synthetic datasets with pixel-wise annotations.
The motives are clear, but the novelty of the proposed methods, verification processes, and datasets is somewhat limited.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper tries to tackle the explanation of the CNN, a.k.a. concept extraction (CE). The main challenge of such task is that there is no universal standard for evaluating the process. The proposed method ECLAD claims to localize concepts and highlight the importance for a single image. As an orthogonal contribution, they also provide a synthetic dataset for quantitatively validating CE techniques by using spatially associating labelled components for evaluation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
One of the contribution of this paper is about a new synthetic dataset which can provide GT information regarding the part relation with the neighborhood. However, the proposed synthetic dataset lacks of justification of the design (weird letters attached to some images) which can hardly claims the dataset is able to provide fair comparison due to its unrealistic nature. This basically put the idea of whole paper in question.

For example, comparing to the baseline ACE, the super-pixels from ACE can be meaningful sometimes like a wheel or human part. However, the patches here are just not meaningful nor comes from a full object. As a human I cannot tell the importance behind analyzing random letters synthetic dataset and I don't see how can this relate to general concept extraction since there is no main concept in each image from the beginning.

In Figure 4, the proposed method also didn't show any significant improvement comparing to the baselines. To this end, I cannot tell the importance of the method nor the dataset.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Overall speaking, I don't think the paper is clear enough.

Comparing to their main competitor Automatic Concept-based Explanations (ACE), the overview diagram is unclear. For example, there are a lot of weird letters on the image patches and with no explanation of the intention. The paper is also not self-contained, many specific terms have been mentioned but not explained, such as TCAV, CAV. 

There is no reasonable motivation behind the dataset design. 

After reading the paper, I cannot tell why ECLAD provides better explanation other than providing a highlight region from an unrealistic dataset which is not very hard to do with any neural network attention visualization.
content.summary_of_the_review: As a summary, I think the idea of the paper is a good idea by providing a synthetic dataset for validating concept extraction (CE). However, the paper is not very well organized, some specific terms are not well described, and the quality of the proposed dataset is not realistic at all. Hence, it's hard to say the proposed method is valuable or not since the standard itself is questionable.

Negative

- From the proposed concept extraction technique ECLAD in figure 1, it is very similar to the previous ACE, though these are a few of the improvements in ECLAD. The improvements of ECLAD are incremental.
- The motivations of this work are unclear. This paper is hard to understand.

content.title: ECLAD: Extracting Concepts with Local Aggregated Descriptors
content.abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are increasingly being used in critical systems, where robustness and alignment are crucial. In this context, the field of explainable artificial intelligence has proposed the generation of high-level explanations of the prediction process of CNNs through concept extraction. While these methods can detect whether or not a concept is present in an image, they are unable to determine its location. What is more, a fair comparison of such approaches is difficult due to a lack of proper validation procedures. To address these issues, we propose a novel method for automatic concept extraction and localization based on representations obtained through pixel-wise aggregations of CNN activation maps. Further, we introduce a process for the validation of concept-extraction techniques based on synthetic datasets with pixel-wise annotations of their main components, reducing the need for human intervention. Extensive experimentation on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates that our method outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives.
